subject: chemistry
title: The mole and the Avogadro constant
key_idea: (AQA: Higher tier) A mole is a fixed number of particles: 6.02 × 10²³, the Avogadro constant. The mass of one mole of a substance in grams is its relative formula mass. This lets you convert between mass, moles and number of particles.

blocks.text: (AQA: Higher tier) Atoms and molecules are far too small to count one by one. Chemists count them in moles instead. This section covers what a mole is.

items.meaning: The unit for the amount of a substance. One mole contains 6.02 × 10²³ particles.
The number of particles in one mole: 6.02 × 10²³ per mole.

items: The particles can be atoms, molecules, ions or formula units.
One mole of any substance contains the same number of particles as one mole of any other substance.
The mass of one mole in grams is **numerically equal** to the relative formula mass (Mr).
One mole has a mass in grams equal to the Mr (or Ar).
The same number of particles in a mole of any substance.

blocks.text: (AQA: Higher tier) Use the Mr to turn a mass in grams into a number of moles, or back again.

blocks.label: Moles
where: Mr = relative formula mass (or Ar for an element)

items.text: 25 000 ÷ 84.3 = 296.56 mol, which is 297 mol to 3 significant figures.

diagram.alt: Practise calculating moles from a mass and a relative formula mass.
diagram.question: Calculate the number of moles in **{m} g** of sodium hydroxide, NaOH. (Ar: Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)

items: Change kg to g first: multiply by 1000.

blocks.text: (AQA: Higher tier) Multiply moles by the Avogadro constant to get the number of particles.

blocks.label: Number of particles
blocks.formula: number of particles = number of moles × 6.02 × 10²³
where: Particles are atoms, molecules, ions or formula units.
Give very large numbers in standard form.

items.text: 72 g of water: Mr = 18, so moles = 72 ÷ 18 = 4.

items: To count atoms, not formula units, multiply by the number of atoms in the formula.
Al₂(SO₄)₃ has 2 + 3 × (1 + 4) = 17 atoms in each formula unit.
The mass of one molecule is the mass of one mole divided by 6.02 × 10²³. For water, 18 ÷ (6.02 × 10²³) = 2.99 × 10⁻²³ g.

diagram.alt: Practise calculating the number of particles from a number of moles.
diagram.question: Calculate the number of atoms in **{n} mol** of copper. Give your answer as a number × 10²³.

items: Find the moles first, then multiply.
For atoms in a compound, multiply by the atoms per formula.

worked_example.question:
Gold is used in the printed circuit boards found in smartphones.

A type of smartphone contains 1.73 × 10⁻⁴ moles of gold.

In one year, a manufacturer sold 2.48 million of this type of smartphone.

Relative atomic mass (Ar): Au = 197

Calculate the total mass of gold contained in 2.48 million of these smartphones.

Give your answer in kilograms.
answer_points: Mass of gold in one phone = 1.73 × 10⁻⁴ × 197 = 0.034081 g
worked_example.tip: Alternatively, find the total moles first (429.04), then multiply by 197 and convert to kilograms.

worked_example.question:
The formula of aluminium sulfate is Al₂(SO₄)₃.

Calculate the total number of atoms that combine to form 5.13 g of aluminium sulfate.

(relative atomic masses: O = 16.0, Al = 27.0, S = 32.0; Avogadro number = 6.02 × 10²³)
answer_points: Atoms in the formula = 17, so atoms = 17 × 0.015 × 6.02 × 10²³ (1)
worked_example.tip: A correct final answer of 1.5351 × 10²³ scores all four marks.

worked_example.question:
The value of the Avogadro constant is 6.02 × 10²³.

Calculate the number of water molecules in 72 g of water, H₂O.

Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
worked_example.tip: The answer 2.41 × 10²⁴ on the answer line scores all three marks.

worked_example.question:
Organic compounds contain hydrogen atoms.

Calculate the number of hydrogen atoms in 44.0 g of the ester methyl propanoate, CH₃CH₂COOCH₃.

One mole of CH₃CH₂COOCH₃ contains 6.02 × 10²³ molecules.

Give your answer in standard form.

blocks.text: (Supplement) You may be asked to find a molar mass, or an unknown Ar or Mr, from a mass and an amount in moles.

items.meaning: The mass of one mole of a substance, in g/mol. It is numerically equal to Mr.

items: 0.0500 mol of an element has a mass of 1.35 g. Molar mass = 1.35 ÷ 0.0500 = 27 g/mol, so Ar = 27.
The same method gives an unknown Mr, and so the identity of a compound.

worked_example.question:
Sodium reacts with water. The equation for the reaction is

2Na(s) + 2H₂O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + H₂(g)

The reaction produces 0.036 g of hydrogen gas.

One mole of hydrogen gas contains 6.0 × 10²³ molecules.

Calculate the number of molecules of hydrogen gas produced in the reaction. Give your answer to two significant figures.
answer_points: Answer to two significant figures = 1.1 × 10²² molecules
worked_example.tip: One mark for the moles, one for multiplying by the Avogadro constant and one for the rounding.
